author: hoeschec
text:
Practice EUR-AUD:

Why did price turn here?

Answer: look left 4 times

Here are the 4 important areas: I will draw each one, starting from # 4 and working my way to the reaction:

I start by finding true supply. Reaction is important, MPL respected. Also notice the trick. Look at the first time price engulfs the MPL of true supply...this is the start of the next FL Box.

FL Box B is formed when price engulfs True Supply "A". This is also the source/DO of the FO.

Next, look for the exact candle that breaks the low of FL Box B...this is the start of a new swap zone and "True Supply" level. True Supply "C" is especially important because it formed after an engulf of a previous Decision to FO...that DP to FO was also the DP to engulf a previous TS zone (TS A).

Price Reacts @ point X to the MPL of True Supply C. Point "X" is not originally formed...it was a reaction to an originally formed Supply zone.

FL Box "D" is still Seller-controlled...the balance of power has not changed to Bulls, so this is a reaction. How do we know if we can trade the fractal TS level formed in Box D? We have to look left and see if price has already visited the MPL of the original TS zone.

Reaction X has already hit the extreme set of orders in the FL contained within TS "C"...we are safe to sell when price RT to the fractal TS level created within FL Box D. That is why price reacts so nicely...

author: hoeschec
text:
A Drawing I made to remind myself of the importance an unmet target is... is increases the odds that we will get a good reaction at a newly formed area of FOF.

In theory, this is a relatively easy concept to understand. The challenging part is executing the trade...

(assuming a short trade setup...it would be the exact opposite for a long trade setup)

The main components you must know for this trade:

1. Find an original true supply/demand zone with good history of price reaction (FL)

2. Watch for a FO above this level (RBD)

3. Draw the FL Box that forms as a result of the engulf of the original true supply zone

4. Draw the DP to FO

5. Draw the EG of the DP to FO

6. Determine the target for the EG of the DP to FO

7. If price returns to the newly created FOF (New TS) prior to hitting the target of the engulf, it is a high probability trade.

Making a mistake on any of the 7 main components above will probably result in a lost trade. I will be keeping track of all my losing trades to find out which of the 7 main steps I need the most practice on.

text: hi Hs, just wanted to say some thing about FOF, it's not about the MPLs or QM LVLs, it's about the ITs scenario. in fact it's about price reading article. you know that some times we have an north eng and we see a south FO. in fact that eng has no difference with FO but it's an ITs intention for future and that south FO is a realized target. some times ITs give their intention before reaching the target and some times after reaching the target. this is important that every ENG has it's own target.FOF is the way that ITs think about moving price it's not about reaching target or not. also it's not about entry points also. hope it makes sense regards Salivan
